inputs.prompt:
The image is a square clean contemporary comic page about a coffee errand, drawn in confident black ink with flat muted colours against white gutters.

In the upper-left panel, a pale green tiled backsplash and a single window set a quiet kitchen scene. A young woman with a short dark bob and blunt fringe, round wire-rimmed glasses, and a small mole on her left cheek stands beside the window. She wears a mustard yellow crew-neck jumper and dark blue jeans, holding an empty white mug and looking into it with a flat expression. A clean white speech balloon with a thin black outline sits above her, its tail pointing toward her, and reads "Out of coffee." in comfortably legible black lettering.

In the upper-right panel, sparse diagonal ink strokes mark the rain on a muted grey street. The same woman, with her bob, glasses, mole, mustard yellow jumper, and dark blue jeans unchanged, walks to the right beneath a transparent umbrella. On the far side, a shop has a green awning; any lettering on its façade is too small to read. A small caption box in the panel’s upper-left corner reads "TWO MINUTES LATER" in clear black capitals.

In the lower-left panel, the café counter runs across the foreground, seen from the barista’s side. The woman faces the viewer from behind the counter, still wearing the same clothes and round glasses, with her dark bob and cheek mole visible. From the right edge, a barista’s arm extends into the frame, offering her a plain paper cup. Her white, black-outlined speech balloon reads "Large, please." and points toward her; a smaller balloon from off-panel right reads "Coming up." with its tail pointing beyond the edge.

In the lower-right panel, the pale green backsplash and single window return, placing the woman in the same spot as in the first panel. Her hair, glasses, mole, mustard yellow jumper, and dark blue jeans remain consistent as she holds the paper cup in both hands. She smiles with her eyes closed, and a white speech balloon with a black outline reads "Better." A small hand-lettered "SIP" sits near the cup in black capitals.

The lighting shifts from soft, cool daylight by the kitchen window to overcast street light and gentle café warmth, then returns to the kitchen’s even daylight, with shadows falling softly behind the figures. The overall composition uses four equal rectangular panels in a strict two-by-two grid, separated by even white gutters and enclosed by thin black borders; its restrained palette and steady ink linework give the page a balanced, calm comic-strip feel.
